matchstick.title: Transform V into X by repositioning one stick
matchstick.principle: A V consists of two diagonal sticks meeting at a point, while an X consists of two diagonal sticks crossing. By moving one of the V's sticks so that it intersects the other, you turn V into X without touching any other symbol. This adds exactly 5 to the numeral's value and often resolves the equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a V appears in a numeral that needs to increase by 5 to balance the equation, consider turning that V into an X by repositioning one of its own sticks.
matchstick.example: Attempting to change V to X by taking a stick from another symbol (e.g., the equals sign), which destroys the source symbol.

matchstick.title: Move a vertical I‑stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: I is a single vertical stick; moving an I‑stick from a numeral that contains multiple I's to another numeral adds 1 to the target and subtracts 1 from the source while keeping both symbols valid. This is useful when the numeric discrepancy between the two sides of the equation is exactly one.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by one and a numeral contains an extra I that can be transferred without leaving the source empty.
matchstick.example: Removing the only I from a numeral, leaving it empty (which is not a valid Roman numeral).

matchstick.title: Prefer intra‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If a single stick can be repositioned within the same character to produce another valid Roman numeral (e.g., V → X), this avoids altering other symbols and reduces the risk of creating invalid characters. Intra‑character moves keep the rest of the equation unchanged and often solve the puzzle with the minimal change.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a character can be transformed into another valid character by moving one of its own sticks, prioritize that over moving sticks between different characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a different numeral to change V into X, which breaks the source numeral.

matchstick.title: Validate source and target symbols after a stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, both the symbol you removed it from and the symbol you added it to must still represent a valid Roman numeral or operator. Removing a stick that leaves a single angled line or adding a stick that creates an illegal shape invalidates the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick move, verify that both affected symbols remain valid according to Roman‑numeral and operator rules.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal stick from X, leaving a single diagonal slash, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid creating single angled sticks (invalid numerals)
matchstick.principle: A lone angled stick does not correspond to any Roman numeral; V and X require two diagonal sticks, and I requires a vertical stick. Moves that leave a solitary diagonal line produce an invalid character and must be rejected.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering removing a diagonal stick from V or X, ensure the remaining shape still forms a valid numeral (e.g., V → I is not allowed).
matchstick.example: Removing one stick from V, leaving a single diagonal line, which is not a valid numeral.
